product_summary: TigerExchange is a self-hosted Research Collaboration Loop Engine for a single research organization (modeled as multiple groups/tenants) running entirely on one NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 64GB with no cloud dependency. Its centerpiece — the position no incumbent occupies — is a CLOSED, COMPOUNDING collaboration loop: (1) a funding opportunity match triggers a 'Pursuit'; (2) the platform assembles a cross-group team from a LIVING expertise graph (two-axis: expertise COVERAGE of the RFP + prior-collaboration CONNECTIVITY, always human-curatable); (3) the team co-authors a CONFIDENTIAL grant proposal grounded in BOTH the shared public scholarly+funding corpus AND the tenant's OWN prior confidential winning proposals (via a per-tenant confidential retrieval surface, never a shared one) inside a per-tenant encrypted CRDT workspace; (4) the funding OUTCOME is recorded; (5) on a WIN, the team, award, and produced artifacts are WRITTEN BACK into the public expertise graph (outcome-weighted, transparently), so every won proposal demonstrably improves the next match. More collaboration -> richer graph -> better matches -> more funding. Incumbents are structurally split across this loop: RIM tools (Pure/Symplectic/VIVO) and Clarivate WoS Research Intelligence own discovery+visibility but stop at the front door; Instrumentl/Granted own drafting but never ground in a shared scholarly corpus and have zero confidentiality controls; IN-PART/AcademicLabs own the introduction then hand off to humans. TigerExchange owns the SEAMS they lack — discovery -> confidential workspace -> outcome capture -> graph write-back — and is the only design that learns from outcomes. We deliberately do NOT compete on funder-database breadth (Pivot-RP 3.6M profiles etc.), unwinnable on one HDD-bound box; our moat is depth-within-tenant corpus grounding + per-tenant cryptographic confidentiality + the outcome-learning loop. Identity aligns to mandatory federal rails (ORCID canonical researcher ID, SciENcv Common Forms biosketch interchange, NIH-required from May 2026) so assembled teams are submission-ready. The compounding loop is empirically validated (collaborators win 2-4x more funding over 10 years; co-authorship 13.8pp more likely after a prior co-proposal, limited to SUCCESSFUL participants), so the value claim is real, not marketing. The build is sequenced as a WALKING SKELETON first: prove the end-to-end loop with the full security spine on the simplest substrate (one tenant pair, real-time editing only, binary allow/quarantine classification, drop-encrypted-tablespace crypto-shred, single embedding space, pgvector HNSW), then add breadth (suggesting mode, anchored comments, HippoRAG2, probabilistic identity resolution, hardware key anchor) in P1.
collaboration_loop_design: The loop is made FIRST-CLASS by (a) a single durable domain object — the Pursuit — threading all five stages, and (b) an explicit, TESTED write-back data flow the v2 plans never wired. STAGE 1 (discover/trigger): mod-funding ingests Grants.gov daily OPPORTUNITIES + NIH-RePORTER/NSF AWARDS; a saved Pursuit (Instrumentl-style project+tracker) binds matched Opportunity -> draft Proposal -> candidate team + ongoing match alerts. Funding is the top-of-loop trigger (concrete need beats aimless expert browsing; rejects discovery-first cold-start). STAGE 2 (team): mod-discovery ranks candidates on TWO axes over the PUBLIC-tier expertise graph — expertise-COVERAGE of the RFP's required concept areas (complementary/gap-filling, shown as a coverage matrix with gaps) AND graph CONNECTIVITY / prior co-authorship+co-funding distance — with an outcome-weighted overlay and per-candidate 'why', and the PI always curates (team-formation literature: algorithm alone produces worse teams). STAGE 3 (co-author): mod-workspace (PROMOTED to first-class) provides editorial modes — WALKING-SKELETON P0 ships REAL-TIME concurrent edit only; suggesting/tracked-changes with PI accept/reject and anchored comments+resolve are P1 — over Notion-style scoped roles (PI=owner, co-PI=edit, reviewer=comment, viewer=view), permission cascade, highest-permission-wins. The live edit buffer is a CRDT (Yjs/y-crdt via pycrdt, aarch64 wheels) served by a self-hosted pycrdt-websocket server. GROUNDING IS DUAL-SOURCE and this resolves the prior STAGE-3-vs-public-only contradiction: mod-lit-intelligence retrieves over (i) the SHARED PUBLIC corpus index (cross-tenant, public-tier only) AND (ii) a PER-TENANT CONFIDENTIAL retrieval surface — a tenant-scoped, RLS-isolated vector+BM25 index living on a per-tenant ENCRYPTED TABLESPACE that holds ONLY that tenant's own confidential drafts and prior winning proposals; the PEP enforces that ONLY that tenant's confidential drafting path can query it (tenant A grounds on A's prior proposals; tenant B physically cannot retrieve them). 'Confidential content never enters any SHARED index' means the cross-tenant public index — NOT that confidential content is unindexable for its owning tenant. The draft is MAX-rule-tagged confidential and periodically snapshotted (AES-256-GCM, per-tenant DEK, non-searchable blob) into the per-tenant KEK-bound encrypted store so crypto-shred reaches it. STAGE 4 (outcome): mod-funding records won/lost/submitted, emitting `proposal.outcome_recorded`. STAGE 5 (write-back, THE CENTERPIECE): a Dagster sensor on the outbox fires an ASYNC enrichment job (off the interactive hot path, semaphore-gated to yield to interactive generation, capped DuckDB/embedding memory, respecting HDD latency) that (i) materializes in-platform CO_PI_WITH edges between actual team members tagged with the proposal/award, (ii) attaches a TRANSPARENT outcome-weighted expertise signal per member for the RFP concepts (ONE signal among similarity+connectivity, to dodge the incumbency-bias trap), (iii) ingests produced artifacts as new public WORK nodes through the SAME classify-gates-index monotonic-applier (idempotent; cannot resurrect revoked/down-classified records). MEASURABILITY: a dedicated NON-security loop-event stream (pursuit_created, opportunity_matched, team_shortlisted, invite_sent, collaborator_joined[cross-tenant], first_co_edit, suggestion_resolved, proposal_submitted, outcome_recorded, graph_enriched) keeps the hash-chained security audit clean; ACTIVATION NORTH-STAR is `collaborator_joined` where joining_tenant != workspace_owner_tenant (a cross-GROUP collaborative act, per Miro/Dropbox aha-moment evidence); loop health = conversion match->team->edit->submit->win + time-to-team + cross-group edit ratio.
architecture_overview: TigerExchange (single-Orin edition) is a MODULAR MONOLITH: one FastAPI application + one Postgres 16 instance + a SMALL FIXED SET of model-serving processes (NOT one all-in-one runtime), all co-resident on a single Jetson AGX Orin 64GB. No Kubernetes, no microservices, no second region, no second box. Layers: (1) the near-frozen `contracts` KERNEL (Tier lattice, PublishableProjection, all I* Protocol interfaces, PEP request/response types) that everything imports and that imports nothing feature-side; (2) the SECURITY KERNEL built first — one IN-PROCESS Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) + data-access broker that is the SOLE chokepoint for every retrieve/egress/derive call (carries v2 D4 forward, collapsed from two PEP loci to one because there is one node); (3) the DATA PLANE — a SINGLE Postgres providing relational tables, pgvector HNSW dense vectors, native BM25 lexical search, RRF in SQL, and a metadata-backbone graph as an edge table traversed by recursive CTEs (this collapses v2's Qdrant+OpenSearch+SpiceDB+Apache-AGE polyglot into ONE engine per the retrieval+security research); the data plane hosts BOTH the shared public retrieval index AND, on per-tenant encrypted tablespaces, the per-tenant confidential retrieval surfaces; (4) the AI plane — THREE small vLLM processes (one for the Qwen3-30B-A3B MoE generator/judge, one embedder, one reranker), each one-model-per-process with its own CUDA context, behind a classification-routed IModelRouter; SPECTER2 is NOT a serve-time process — its citation-aware embeddings are PRECOMPUTED AT INGEST and the model is unloaded before serving; (5) FEATURE MODULES as 'dumb' plug-ins behind the PEP: mod-discovery (team assembly), mod-lit-intelligence (dual-source proposal grounding), mod-workspace (confidential CRDT co-authoring — PROMOTED to first-class Phase-0, the centerpiece), mod-funding (opportunity+award feeds); (6) the LOOP ENGINE — an async Dagster write-back job that, on a recorded WON outcome, re-ingests team+award+artifacts through the same classify-gates-index pipeline to re-weight the expertise graph, closing the compounding loop. Tenants = research groups on one box, isolated by FORCE-RLS + transaction-scoped SET LOCAL + per-tenant DEK-on-encrypted-tablespace + per-tenant KEK envelope crypto for non-searchable blobs. Storage tiered: HDD = cold sequential archive of raw CC0 snapshots ONLY; attached NVMe (effectively mandatory in BOM) = hot tier for Postgres data/WAL, live vector/BM25/graph indexes, Parquet working sets; RAM = transient + model weights + index hot pages. CONCURRENCY IS PHASE-PARTITIONED (no triple-counted headroom): the box runs in exactly one of three mutually-exclusive memory regimes at a time — SERVE (interactive), INGEST-WINDOW (bulk DuckDB load with serving paused / shared_buffers reduced), WRITEBACK-WINDOW (semaphore-gated async enrichment yielding to interactive generation). All cross-BOX federation (central network read-PEP, tombstone-bitmap replication, broker DPoP tokens, cross-node schema negotiation, distributed tuple resolution, SpiceDB replication) is DEFERRED behind clean kernel Protocol seams (IExchangeFeed, IRevocationAuthority, PublishableProjection.discoverability_scope); the future-federation doc is HONEST that two single-box mechanisms (volume/tablespace crypto-shred and local-only CTE ReBAC resolution) are KNOWN federation-boundary REWRITES, not transport swaps.

tech_stack.choice: Jetson AGX Orin 64GB, JetPack 6.2 (L4T r36.4.3), CUDA 12.6, Ubuntu 22.04 aarch64, Python 3.11+, power mode MAXN, GPU SM 8.7 (Ampere)
tech_stack.rationale: Fixed hardware. PIN this verbatim in the runbook. ALL CUDA Python wheels (torch, vLLM, flash-attn, xformers, bitsandbytes) MUST come from https://pypi.jetson-ai-lab.io/jp6/cu126 — default PyPI cu126 wheels omit SM 8.7 SASS and will fail or silently fall to CPU (the #1 Jetson LLM failure mode).
tech_stack.fallback: If JetPack 6.2 unavailable, JetPack 6.1 (CUDA 12.6) is the documented alternate; never downgrade below CUDA 12.6 or the pinned wheels break.

tech_stack.choice: Qwen3-30B-A3B (MoE, 30.5B total / 3.3B active) at W4A16 AWQ or GPTQ-Int4, served in ONE shared vLLM process for ALL tenants
tech_stack.rationale: MoE activation sparsity makes decode bandwidth-bound at ~3B speed (~30-45 tok/s on Orin) at near-32B quality, with strong grounded-RAG + structured output. Resident ~17GB at INT4. CRITICAL: there is only ONE resident copy — confidential isolation is achieved WITHOUT a second model copy (see D10), because a second resident 30B (~17GB weights + ~4-8GB context) would push the total to ~70GB > 64GB. Chose over dense Qwen2.5-32B (~19GB Q4 AND slower dense decode), Mixtral 8x7B, Gemma3-27B dense, Llama-3.x-70B.
tech_stack.fallback: Qwen3-14B dense (~9GB weights at INT4) — used BOTH if the A3B MoE quant misbehaves AND as the model loaded by an optional dedicated confidential process (with the public 30B PAUSED/EVICTED, never both 30B copies resident).

tech_stack.choice: vLLM (jetson-ai-lab PyTorch index + community SM 8.7 GPTQ-Marlin/AWQ INT4 wheel, pin vLLM >=0.10.x) run as THREE SEPARATE PROCESSES: (1) `vllm serve` for the LLM, (2) a pooling/embedding process, (3) a score/reranker process — each one-model-per-process with its own CUDA context
tech_stack.rationale: +30-40% decode and 3.8x faster prefill vs llama.cpp, OpenAI-compatible API, zero per-model compile. CORRECTION FROM PRIOR DRAFT: vLLM is strictly ONE model per process; it cannot host the generator AND embedder AND reranker in a single instance, so 'one runtime' = the same software run as 3 processes (3 CUDA contexts, ~1.3GB context each, all counted in the memory budget). This is still operationally simpler than three DIFFERENT serving systems and still closes the Ollama reranker gap (Ollama has NO /api/rerank as of 2026).
tech_stack.fallback: 1 vLLM process for the LLM + sentence-transformers IN-PROCESS for embed/rerank — avoids two extra CUDA contexts (~2.6GB) and may be lighter on Orin; this is the RECOMMENDED memory-saving variant if the 3-process budget is tight. Ollama is dev-time-only for the LLM, never the reranker.

tech_stack.choice: bge-m3 (dense+sparse+ColBERT, 8192 ctx, 568M) OR Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B as the SINGLE serve-time retriever embedder
tech_stack.rationale: Small (137M-568M), coexists with the 30B generator in 64GB; bge-m3's single-model multi-representation simplifies the hybrid stack. Chose over Qwen3-Embedding-8B (MTEB #1 but 8B resident not worth it on a shared box).
tech_stack.fallback: nomic-embed-text (137M) if even 568M is tight; serve via sentence-transformers if vLLM pooling misbehaves.

tech_stack.layer: Citation-aware expertise embedding (SPECTER2) — INGEST-ONLY, NOT serve-resident
tech_stack.choice: SPECTER2 (Apache-2.0) base + PROXIMITY adapter via the `adapters` (adapter-transformers) library on the SM 8.7 PyTorch wheel, run as a BATCH job at ingest to PRECOMPUTE ExpertiseFingerprint / paper-similarity vectors, then UNLOADED
tech_stack.rationale: SPECTER2 beats general models on citation-proximity, directly powering collaborator discovery — but it is a REQUIRED SECOND embedding space the budget must account for. CORRECTION: it is an adapter on SciBERT (bert-base) requiring the proximity adapter loaded on the base; it is NOT a drop-in sentence-transformers model and is NOT served by vLLM pooling. Precomputing at ingest (then unloading, ~0GB at serve) is the right call on this box — its ~0.5-1GB footprint + the adapter library appear only in the INGEST-WINDOW budget, never serve-time.
tech_stack.fallback: If the `adapters` library is troublesome on aarch64, fall back to using bge-m3 embeddings for the connectivity/similarity axis at reduced citation-precision; SPECTER2 then becomes a P1 enhancement.

tech_stack.choice: bge-reranker-v2-m3 (568M) OR Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B, served via a DEDICATED vLLM score-endpoint process (its own CUDA context, counted in budget)
tech_stack.rationale: Lightweight, multilingual, +5-15 nDCG@10 for <200ms. Chose over Ollama (no rerank endpoint) and large rerankers (won't fit hot beside the 30B).
tech_stack.fallback: sentence-transformers CrossEncoder in-process on the SM 8.7 PyTorch wheel (avoids the third CUDA context — the recommended saver).

tech_stack.choice: SINGLE Postgres 16: relational tables + pgvector HNSW (dense) + native BM25 (VectorChord-BM25 with ParadeDB pg_search as co-equal alternate) + RRF in SQL + edge-table graph via recursive CTE
tech_stack.rationale: One memory-shared Orin with a slow HDD cannot afford Qdrant + OpenSearch + SpiceDB + Apache-AGE as extra always-on services competing for the 64GB the models need. CORRECTION: VectorChord-BM25 DOES support aarch64 with SVE SIMD + runtime CPU dispatch (and ARM64 benchmarks competitively), but we DO NOT lean on any inherited x86 '3x-vs-Elasticsearch' number as the single-box rationale — the only rationale that matters here is one-engine consolidation. Native-BM25 Postgres extensions are production-grade; one transactional store makes per-tenant RLS isolation and tablespace-level crypto-shred dramatically simpler for a 30B builder. REVISES v2's locked Qdrant+OpenSearch and Apache-AGE choices for the single-box edition.
tech_stack.fallback: pgvector HNSW is the VERIFIED P0 dense default; ParadeDB pg_search is a co-equal verified BM25 alternate if VectorChord's Rust extension won't build on the JetPack base. Qdrant/OpenSearch adapters are kept ONLY as documented future scale-out, not P0.

tech_stack.layer: Disk-friendly vector index (P1 upgrade path ONLY, not P0 load-bearing)
tech_stack.choice: VectorChord IVF+RaBitQ / DiskANN-style (~1-bit quantized codes) — a P1 'verify-then-adopt' task, NOT a P0 dependency; pgvector HNSW kept RAM-resident is the P0 default
tech_stack.rationale: Scans bit-packed quantized codes instead of float vectors, attractive IF the index ever exceeds RAM. CORRECTION: the P0 design REQUIRES the live index to fit RAM/NVMe regardless (HNSW off HDD = 10s+ queries), so the '>RAM index via RaBitQ' story is NOT load-bearing for P0 and is moved entirely to P1 after on-aarch64 verification. HNSW is pure random I/O and catastrophic off HDD, so whichever index is chosen MUST stay RAM-resident / on NVMe.
tech_stack.fallback: pgvector HNSW (compiles cleanly on aarch64, ARM-optimized distance kernels) kept RAM-resident — the P0 default, no upgrade required.

tech_stack.choice: CRDT via Yjs/y-crdt (pycrdt, successor to y-py) with a self-hosted pycrdt-websocket / Hocuspocus-style server on the Orin; CRDT doc is the live buffer, snapshotted (AES-256-GCM, non-searchable blob) into the KEK-bound draft store
tech_stack.rationale: CRDT merges in any order, survives server restart, supports offline edit + autosave recovery (Notion/Figma model), fully self-hostable on one box. Chose over Operational Transformation (requires central server, worse offline/recovery) and last-write-wins (silently loses concurrent edits).
tech_stack.fallback: If pycrdt's aarch64 wheel breaks, build y-crdt from Rust source on the box; the CRDT doc per proposal is KB-MB so the constraint is never the CRDT.

tech_stack.choice: IN-PROCESS Python inside the single PEP using the kernel lattice (tier_join_all MAX-rule, Entitlement.permits_tier, caveats re-evaluated at access)
tech_stack.rationale: The ABAC ruleset is a tiny FIXED 3-tier lattice + capability gate — a few lines of fail-closed Python beat standing up a policy engine; nothing to sync, nothing to operate, impossible for a module to bypass (lives inside the PEP). REVISES v2/CONVENTIONS 'ABAC=OPA' for the single-box edition (no Go daemon).
tech_stack.fallback: None needed — it is pure Python; OPA stays a documented considered-alternative only.

tech_stack.choice: Postgres-native relation-tuple table (subject, relation, object, tenant_id) evaluated by a recursive-CTE Check() function in the SAME Postgres, behind the kernel IPolicyEnforcement/relation-Check Protocol
tech_stack.rationale: Zanzibar's tuple model maps to one indexed Postgres table; recursive CTEs evaluate nested relations fast with proper indexes; zero new infra, tuples inherit tenant RLS isolation, pure Python+SQL. REVISES v2/CONVENTIONS 'ReBAC=SpiceDB' for the single-box edition. HONEST CAVEAT: the recursive-CTE Check resolves LOCAL tables only — cross-box federation needs distributed tuple resolution this cannot do, so this is a KNOWN federation-boundary rewrite (documented in 15-future), NOT a clean transport swap.
tech_stack.fallback: None needed (pure SQL); SpiceDB stays a documented future-federation alternative behind the unchanged Protocol.

tech_stack.choice: Dependency-free in-process LocalKms behind the kernel IKms Protocol holding per-tenant KEKs encrypted under ONE box-master key. P0 DEFAULT box-master anchoring = fTPM via the userspace tpm2-tools/tpm2-pytss stack (seal to a PCR) OR a passphrase-derived master key entered at boot (NIST SP 800-108 KDF, key never on disk). destroy_kek() = crypto-shred.
tech_stack.rationale: CORRECTION: the OP-TEE/EKB secure-world anchor is NOT turnkey — it requires irreversible OEM fuse-burning + Secure Boot provisioning + a custom OP-TEE Trusted Application in C, and NVIDIA's own forums show unresolved EKB/SSK derivation failures. That is firmware/secure-world C engineering far beyond a Python-writing 30B builder and a likely hard build wall. So the Phase-0 builder default is the USERSPACE fTPM (tpm2-tools, no custom TA) or passphrase-KDF path. This still REPLACES v2's CloudHSM/cloud-KMS seam (wrong for a no-cloud box). Chose over raw key file (master key plaintext on slow HDD — unacceptable).
tech_stack.fallback: OP-TEE/EKB hardware anchor documented as an OPTIONAL human-operator hardening step (irreversible fuse-burn, OUT OF SCOPE for the automated build) behind the SAME IKms; OpenBao Transit as an optional stronger backend.

tech_stack.choice: Per-tenant ENCRYPTED TABLESPACE / LUKS-dm-crypt volume holding the tenant's confidential vector + BM25 + graph indexes; crypto-shred = DESTROY the per-tenant DEK that unlocks that volume (then drop-and-rebuild)
tech_stack.rationale: CORRECTION (was inverted in the prior draft): AES-256-GCM application-layer encryption on vectors/BM25 postings is MATHEMATICALLY incompatible with searching them — AES ciphertext destroys the distance metric pgvector/HNSW need and encrypted postings cannot be tokenized/scored. Therefore volume/tablespace-level encryption is the PRIMARY (not fallback) crypto-shred mechanism for ALL searchable confidential derivatives: the index data stays plaintext-AT-REST-INSIDE an encrypted block device, searchable while mounted, and crypto-shredded by destroying the unlocking DEK. This is node-local (a KNOWN federation-boundary rewrite, see 15-future).
tech_stack.fallback: Per-tenant logical Postgres tablespace + DROP on shred where full LUKS-per-tenant is impractical; physical scrub as last resort.

tech_stack.choice: AES-256-GCM via the `cryptography` library, per-tenant DEK, applied ONLY to non-searchable at-rest blobs: CRDT draft snapshots, autosave, version history, eval traces, cache VALUES
tech_stack.rationale: CORRECTION: ALE is the right mechanism EXACTLY where the data is never searched (opaque blobs), and the WRONG mechanism for indexes. Scoping ALE to non-searchable blobs makes crypto-shred reach drafts/history/eval while leaving searchable indexes to tablespace-level crypto-shred. ARM64-trivial. Rejected homomorphic/searchable/distance-preserving encryption (research-grade, x86-tuned, beyond a 30B builder).
tech_stack.fallback: None needed for blobs; the searchable-index path is handled entirely by the encrypted-tablespace mechanism above.

tech_stack.choice: DuckDB (out-of-core, spill-to-disk) reading gzip-JSONL/NDJSON directly -> writing Parquet on NVMe, with SET memory_limit (e.g. 8GB) and capped threads EXPLICITLY set
tech_stack.rationale: Native aarch64 build, reads gzip NDJSON natively, spills to disk so it processes the >RAM OpenAlex/Crossref sets on a 64GB box without loading into RAM. CORRECTION: DuckDB still wants several GB working RAM for hash joins/sorts, so its memory_limit is CAPPED and it runs only in the INGEST-WINDOW or semaphore-gated WRITEBACK-WINDOW — never silently concurrent with full serving. Chose over Spark (heavy), Pandas (won't fit), hand-rolled streamers.
tech_stack.fallback: pyarrow streaming as a thin alternate for tiny sources.

tech_stack.choice: Dagster (pin dagster>=1.8,<2) for the classify-gates-index ingestion DAGs + the transactional-outbox sensor that triggers the semaphore-gated async loop write-back job
tech_stack.rationale: Correct minimalist substrate for one box, already in the TigerBuddy stack; outbox-polling avoids Kafka/Temporal/Debezium. Chose over Temporal/Kafka CDC (scale machinery) and ad-hoc cron (no lineage, no sensor model).
tech_stack.fallback: Plain Python + systemd timers if Dagster's aarch64 install is troublesome, but Dagster is the documented default.

tech_stack.choice: FastAPI (latest 0.11x) + asyncpg + SQLAlchemy 2 + PgBouncer (transaction mode); tenant context pinned per-transaction via set_config('app.tenant_id', <bound param>, true) (SET LOCAL)
tech_stack.rationale: All first-class aarch64. SET LOCAL (not SET SESSION) is mandatory under PgBouncer transaction mode or the previous tenant's context leaks to the next request on a reused connection; bound parameter avoids tenant-id SQL injection.

tech_stack.choice: Next.js + React (served from the box) connecting to FastAPI; CRDT client (y-websocket) for the workspace editor; force-graph for the expertise-graph/coverage views
tech_stack.rationale: Matches the existing TigerBuddy frontend stack; the editor needs a real CRDT-aware client. Kept deliberately thin — the box's scarce resources go to models, not the UI tier.
tech_stack.fallback: A Streamlit app for an internal/admin surface if the Next.js build is too heavy to host on-box (build off-box, serve static).

decisions.title: Product category = Research Collaboration Loop Engine (not a RIM, funding DB, or grant writer)
decisions.decision: Position and build TigerExchange as the integrated, outcome-learning collaboration loop (discover -> assemble -> confidentially co-author -> win -> feed outcomes back), explicitly NOT as another research-information-management system, funding database, or standalone grant-writing assistant.
decisions.rationale: Every adjacent category has an entrenched data-moat or workflow incumbent; the ONE position no one occupies is the integrated loop that learns from funding outcomes, empirically validated (collaborators win 2-4x more funding over 10 years). This is the user's stated centerpiece.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Better funding database (lose on breadth + HDD/single-box limits vs Pivot-RP/WoS-RI/Instrumentl); standalone AI grant writer (commoditized — Instrumentl Apply drafts in 5 min); VIVO-style RIM (mature, low-growth, maintenance-fatigued).
decisions.consequences: The build must wire the write-back EDGE (Stage 5), which v2 omitted; success metrics are loop-conversion + cross-group activation, not search volume; we accept being narrow-corpus by design.

decisions.title: Single-box modular monolith; cross-BOX federation deferred behind clean seams (with HONEST carry-forward annotations)
decisions.decision: Build a modular monolith (one FastAPI deployable, in-process module boundaries, in-process event bus) on ONE Orin. Tenants = groups/institutions. Design — but do NOT build — cross-box federation behind kernel Protocol seams (IExchangeFeed, IRevocationAuthority, PublishableProjection.discoverability_scope). The future-federation doc explicitly lists which seams carry forward cleanly vs which are single-box-only semantics.
decisions.rationale: The deploy target is literally one box; microservices/K8s/multi-region waste the scarce 64GB. Clean seams make MUCH of the future layer a transport addition. CORRECTION: not EVERYTHING is 'just a transport addition' — see consequences.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Build multi-box federation now (out of scope, premature, high risk for a 30B builder); single-tenant with no seams (forces a rewrite to federate); independently-deployed microservices (K8s overhead the box cannot afford).
decisions.consequences: Collapse v2's dual PEP into ONE in-process PEP. HONESTLY FLAG as KNOWN federation-boundary REWRITES (not transport swaps): (1) crypto-shred-by-encrypted-volume is node-local — a future IRevocationAuthority CANNOT crypto-shred another node's tablespace; (2) the recursive-CTE ReBAC resolves LOCAL tables only — federation needs distributed tuple resolution. Carry-forward-clean: PublishableProjection.discoverability_scope, IExchangeFeed, owner-authoritative re-derivation.

decisions.title: Single Policy Enforcement Point + data-access broker is the sole confidentiality chokepoint
decisions.decision: All retrieve/egress/derive flows through ONE in-process PEP + broker. Feature modules receive already-projected, already-tier-checked objects; they NEVER import the raw store, classifier engine, or construct a PublishableProjection (import-linter + AST test enforced). The broker holds raw-store credentials ONLY for the shared confidential-artifact/classification tables AND per-tenant confidential-index access, NOT every module's schema.
decisions.rationale: On one box every group's data shares the same disk/process, so a single chokepoint is MORE important. New capabilities inherit enforcement for free. Scoping broker creds to shared+confidential tables (not module schemas) resolves the v2 'broker-as-god-object vs module-owns-its-data' contradiction.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Per-module re-implementation of confidentiality mechanisms (a 30B builder will get one wrong = leak); broker holding creds to every module schema (re-centralized coupling); query-time post-filtering only (leaves confidential content in the shared index = standing breach).
decisions.consequences: PEP is built FIRST; decision order is fixed (D4); the broker also gates the per-tenant confidential retrieval surface so only the owning tenant's drafting path can query it (D6/STAGE-3 fix).

decisions.title: Fixed fail-closed PEP decision order with in-Python ABAC and Postgres-CTE ReBAC
decisions.decision: PolicyEnforcementPoint.authorize() runs a single fixed order, cheap-first, fail-closed (any step that errors or abstains DENIES): (1) entitlement/edition gate, (2) capability gate, (3) ABAC tier check (in-process Python lattice), (4) ReBAC relation Check (Postgres recursive CTE), (5) owner-local durable tombstone read (AUTHORITATIVE deny), (6) short-TTL lease (narrow-only positive cache). Caches are narrow-only; the durable log is authoritative for deny.
decisions.rationale: The convergence report's #1 finding was that three stores gating one decision with undefined composition is a fail-OPEN risk; one stated order + durable-log-authoritative-deny + narrow-only caches removes the ambiguity a 30B builder would resolve unsafely. In-Python ABAC and Postgres-CTE ReBAC eliminate the OPA Go daemon and SpiceDB cluster while keeping the same decision semantics behind the kernel Protocol.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: OPA/Rego ABAC (Go daemon, Rego, data-sync — overkill for a fixed 3-tier lattice); SpiceDB/OpenFGA-as-service (high single-node complexity, separate datastore+operator, Go); undefined multi-store composition (fail-open risk).
decisions.consequences: REVISES CONVENTIONS 'ABAC=OPA / ReBAC=SpiceDB'; both engines in-box for P0; IPolicyEnforcement Protocol is the federation seam (but CTE Check is local-only — a federation rewrite, see D2). A HUMAN, not the 30B builder, authors the adversarial CI gates that encode this order.

decisions.title: Per-tenant isolation = FORCE-RLS + RESTRICTIVE + WITH CHECK + SET LOCAL + tenant_id-leading index, with a 4th VIEW guard
decisions.decision: Every tenant-scoped table uses FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY + AS RESTRICTIVE policy FOR ALL with BOTH USING and WITH CHECK on current_setting('app.tenant_id', true), tenant_id as the LEADING index column, set transaction-scoped via set_config(...,true). The app connects as a NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS/NOINHERIT non-owner role. Forbid SECURITY DEFINER, MATERIALIZED VIEWs, AND VIEWs over tenant tables unless created with security_invoker=true.
decisions.rationale: Directly load-bearing for multi-group collaboration on one shared Postgres. FORCE closes owner-bypass; RESTRICTIVE prevents future migrations widening access; WITH CHECK blocks cross-tenant writes; SET LOCAL is leak-proof under PgBouncer transaction pooling; leading tenant_id index makes the predicate an index seek (critical on the HDD box). The VIEW guard is a 3rd bypass vector v2's lint missed.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Schema-per-tenant / database-per-tenant (migration sprawl / resource-prohibitive on one 64GB box); PERMISSIVE policies (OR-combined, accidentally widened); session-level SET (leaks tenant across pooled connections); omitting WITH CHECK (write-side cross-tenant leak/poisoning).
decisions.consequences: Extend check_rls_bypass.py CI lint to flag non-security_invoker views; add a regression test asserting a transaction with NO SET LOCAL returns ZERO rows; add a CI probe that the app role is NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS. The per-tenant confidential retrieval surface (D6) is also RLS-isolated by this exact mechanism.

decisions.title: Classify-gates-index for the SHARED index; per-tenant CONFIDENTIAL retrieval surface for own-tenant grounding
decisions.decision: A record is classified BEFORE it can be embedded/indexed/graphed. Only ClassificationResult.is_retrievable (Decision.ALLOW, public-tier) records reach the SHARED CROSS-TENANT index (vector/BM25/graph/outbox). Classifier abstention/ambiguity -> QUARANTINE (unclassified = treated confidential) -> human adjudication queue. SEPARATELY, each tenant's OWN confidential drafts + prior winning proposals ARE indexed into a PER-TENANT CONFIDENTIAL retrieval surface (tenant-scoped, RLS-isolated, on a per-tenant encrypted tablespace) that ONLY that tenant's confidential drafting path can query (PEP-enforced). The PublishableProjection validator still rejects the confidential tier so confidential content can never be CONSTRUCTED for the SHARED index.
decisions.rationale: CORRECTION resolving the STAGE-3 contradiction: 'confidential content never enters any SHARED index' meant the CROSS-TENANT public index — it must NOT mean confidential content is unindexable for its OWNING tenant, or the centerpiece moat (grounding drafts in the tenant's own prior winning proposals) is non-functional. A per-tenant confidential surface, isolated by RLS + encrypted tablespace + PEP, indexes own-tenant confidential content for own-tenant retrieval only. Structural fail-closed classification at the SHARED edge remains for cross-tenant content.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Query-time post-filtering on a single shared index (leaves confidential content cross-tenant-visible = standing breach); making confidential content wholly unindexable (kills STAGE-3 grounding = the moat); classifier fail-open on low confidence (violates fail-closed).
decisions.consequences: mod-discovery + the expertise graph remain PUBLIC-tier-only by construction; mod-lit-intelligence grounds on TWO surfaces (shared public + own-tenant confidential); P0.9 test: tenant A grounds on A's prior proposal, tenant B cannot retrieve it; the confidential surface lives on the encrypted tablespace whose DEK destruction is the crypto-shred (D7).

decisions.title: Per-tenant crypto-shred: encrypted-tablespace DEK destruction for SEARCHABLE derivatives; AES-GCM ALE for NON-searchable blobs; fTPM/passphrase-anchored master key
decisions.decision: Crypto-shred is split by searchability. (A) SEARCHABLE confidential derivatives (per-tenant vector/BM25/graph indexes) live on a PER-TENANT ENCRYPTED TABLESPACE / LUKS volume; crypto-shred = destroy the per-tenant DEK unlocking that volume, then drop-and-rebuild. (B) NON-searchable confidential blobs (CRDT draft snapshots, autosave, version history, eval traces, cache values) get application-layer AES-256-GCM under the per-tenant DEK before insert. The per-tenant KEK wraps the DEK; the box-master key (wrapping KEKs) is anchored by the P0 DEFAULT fTPM-via-tpm2-tools (seal-to-PCR) OR passphrase-derived KDF (key never on disk). destroy_kek() = O(1) crypto-shred. A post-shred zero-decryptable-hits CI gate proves erasure across BOTH paths.
decisions.rationale: CORRECTION of two prior errors. (1) AES-GCM on vectors/BM25 is mathematically impossible to search (ciphertext destroys distance metrics; encrypted postings cannot be tokenized/scored), so the prior 'ALE on vectors before insert' instruction would produce a broken or insecure system — encrypted-volume + DEK-destroy is the ONLY workable crypto-shred for searchable indexes and is now PRIMARY (was wrongly labeled fallback). (2) The OP-TEE/EKB hardware anchor is NOT turnkey (irreversible fuse-burn + secure-world C TA + documented unresolved NVIDIA-forum failures) — far beyond a Python 30B builder — so the P0 default is the userspace fTPM/passphrase path. Envelope crypto-shred remains O(1) and provable vs O(records x engines) physical deletion.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: ALE-on-searchable-derivatives (unsearchable or insecure — the inverted prior design); CloudHSM/cloud-KMS (contradicts no-cloud single box); OP-TEE/EKB as a Phase-0 BUILD deliverable (firmware C + irreversible fuse-burn = a hard wall for the builder, demoted to optional human hardening); per-record physical deletion across engines (unprovable, races); raw key file (master key plaintext on slow HDD).
decisions.consequences: P0.4 SPLITS into P0.4a (KEK/DEK + LocalKms + fTPM/passphrase anchor + AES-GCM blob encryption — NO store dependency) and P0.4b (per-tenant encrypted tablespace + DEK-destroy crypto-shred of search indexes — runs AFTER the data plane P0.5 exists). OP-TEE/EKB documented in 06/15 as optional human hardening behind the same IKms; OpenBao Transit optional stronger backend.

decisions.title: Retrieval = single-Postgres hybrid (pgvector + native-BM25 + RRF) -> local cross-encoder rerank; verified-on-aarch64 default, no inherited x86 claims
decisions.decision: P0 retrieval is two-stage behind ONE IRetrievalStrategy: Stage 1 hybrid dense (pgvector HNSW — the VERIFIED P0 default) + native BM25 (VectorChord-BM25 or ParadeDB pg_search, whichever benchmarks well on actual aarch64) fused with RRF k=60 in SQL; Stage 2 local cross-encoder rerank top-50 -> top-8. VectorChord IVF+RaBitQ '>RAM index' is a P1 verify-then-adopt task, NOT a P0 dependency. ALL of IVectorStore/ILexicalIndex/IGraph are backed by the single Postgres. A P0.5 acceptance test BENCHMARKS BM25 latency on real aarch64 (no inherited x86 number).
decisions.rationale: Two-stage hybrid+rerank is the evidence-backed quality floor (Recall@5 0.816 vs 0.695 single-stage); BM25 is mandatory for entity-heavy scholarly+grant queries; RRF needs zero labels (correct for a fresh deployment). All-in-Postgres avoids extra always-on services competing for the 64GB. CORRECTION: VectorChord-BM25 supports aarch64 (SVE SIMD, runtime dispatch) and benchmarks competitively, but the single-box rationale is one-engine consolidation + isolation simplicity, NOT any x86 '3x-vs-ES' figure; and the disk-friendly RaBitQ upgrade is deliberately de-risked to P1.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Qdrant+OpenSearch+RRF (two extra services on a memory-shared box — demote to future adapters); vector-only RAG (misses exact entities); learned/convex fusion (needs per-tenant labels you won't have at launch); skipping rerank (leaves the cheapest large quality win on the table); making RaBitQ a P0 dependency (unverified on the target).
decisions.consequences: The live HNSW index MUST stay RAM-resident / on NVMe; graph is an edge table + recursive CTE (no Apache AGE); HippoRAG2 PPR is a P1 SQL add; the per-tenant confidential surface (D6) reuses this exact two-stage pipeline on its own encrypted tablespace.

decisions.title: vLLM is the serving SOFTWARE, run as THREE processes (LLM + embedder + reranker); Qwen3-30B-A3B in ONE shared generator process
decisions.decision: Use vLLM (jetson-ai-lab SM 8.7 wheel path, pinned versions) as the serving software, run as THREE separate one-model-per-process instances: (1) the Qwen3-30B-A3B INT4 generator (ONE shared instance for all tenants), (2) an embedder pooling process, (3) a reranker score process. SPECTER2 is NOT served — precomputed at ingest. Plan latency SLOs against ~30 tok/s decode + ~2000 tok/s prefill.
decisions.rationale: Best decode (+30-40% vs llama.cpp), 3.8x faster prefill, OpenAI-compatible. CORRECTION: vLLM is ONE model per process — a single instance CANNOT host generator+embedder+reranker, so 'one runtime' means the same software as 3 processes, each with its own CUDA context (~1.3GB each), ALL counted in the memory budget. The A3B MoE keeps decode bandwidth-bound at ~3B speed where a dense 32B would crawl. The RECOMMENDED memory-saver is 1 vLLM (LLM) + sentence-transformers in-process for embed/rerank (avoids 2 extra CUDA contexts).
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Single vLLM instance hosting all three models (impossible — one model per process); TensorRT-LLM (30-90 min per-model engine compile, Jetson support preview-grade); MLC-LLM (weak prefill on Jetson); Ollama for prod (NO /api/rerank as of 2026) — dev-only; dense Qwen2.5-32B (slower decode + ~19GB).
decisions.consequences: Pin JetPack 6.2/CUDA 12.6/Python 3.11/SM 8.7 wheels verbatim; NEVER pip install vllm from default PyPI; the memory table has explicit line items for all 3 CUDA contexts + weights; confidential isolation does NOT add a second 30B copy (D10).

decisions.title: Confidential-tenant KV isolation WITHOUT a second model copy: one shared generator, prefix-caching disabled + KV flush for confidential requests
decisions.decision: Confidential drafting runs on the SAME single shared Qwen3-30B-A3B vLLM process as everything else. KV-cache isolation is achieved by (a) disabling prefix caching for confidential requests (--enable-prefix-caching=False on that path) so no prefix/KV is shared across requests, and (b) strict request serialization with a KV-cache boundary between confidential and non-confidential requests. NO per-confidential-tenant model duplication. MIG is unavailable on Orin Ampere and is deferred to a future Thor/Blackwell interface only.
decisions.rationale: CRITICAL CORRECTION: a dedicated vLLM PROCESS per confidential tenant would require a SECOND FULL resident copy of the 30B (~17GB weights + ~4-8GB context), pushing the steady-state total from ~49GB to ~70GB > 64GB — the centerpiece path could not run. vLLM does NOT leak KV across separate requests by default; the real cross-request leak vector is shared-prefix caching, which we disable for confidential requests. So one shared process + prefix-caching-off + serialization is both SAFE and FITS. The Ampere GPU has no MIG regardless.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Dedicated vLLM process per confidential tenant with its own 30B copy (exceeds 64GB by ~6GB minimum — the prior design's fatal arithmetic error); shared in-process vLLM WITH prefix caching enabled for confidential requests (shared-prefix KV leak risk); MIG partition (physically unavailable on AGX Orin).
decisions.consequences: If true PROCESS isolation is ever mandated, the confidential process loads the SMALLER Qwen3-14B (~9GB) AND the public 30B is PAUSED/EVICTED first — NEVER two 30B copies resident; the memory budget proves both regimes fit. Confidential drafting requests are queued/serialized; backpressure exposed to the editor.

decisions.title: mod-workspace (confidential CRDT co-authoring) is PROMOTED to first-class Phase-0; walking-skeleton = real-time edit only
decisions.decision: Build mod-workspace NOW as a first-class Phase-0 capability. WALKING-SKELETON P0 ships REAL-TIME concurrent edit only over Notion-style scoped roles on a CRDT (pycrdt) buffer snapshotted (AES-GCM blob) into the per-tenant KEK-bound draft store. Suggesting/tracked-changes (PI accept/reject) and anchored comments+resolve are P1.
decisions.rationale: Confidential cross-group co-authoring IS the project's centerpiece — deferring it guts the loop. CORRECTION for builder tractability: shipping ALL three editorial modes + scoped roles + cascade in P0 is too large for a 30B builder; real-time edit alone proves the cross-group aha-moment (the activation north-star) and the confidential-snapshot + revocation security path. The kernel seams (IGrantStore, IRevocationAuthority, IAuditSink, MAX-rule drafts) are built against from P0.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Keeping mod-workspace at Phase-1+ (leaves the loop open, centerpiece unbuilt); shipping all three editorial modes in P0 (too much surface for a 30B builder to get the confidentiality right); a read-only 'comment' workspace (no true co-authoring — no aha-moment).
decisions.consequences: CRDT websocket server + KEK snapshotting are Phase-0; draft/autosave/history inherit MAX-rule confidential tier and persist only in encrypted stores; suggesting-mode + anchored comments move to P1 with their own loop events.

decisions.title: The compounding write-back edge is a first-class, tested, memory-gated async data flow
decisions.decision: On `proposal.outcome_recorded` (won), a SEMAPHORE-GATED async Dagster job (yielding to interactive generation, with CAPPED DuckDB/embedding memory) re-ingests the team, award, and produced artifacts through the SAME classify-gates-index monotonic-applier pipeline: materialize in-platform CO_PI_WITH edges, attach a TRANSPARENT outcome-weighted expertise signal (one signal among similarity+connectivity), add artifacts as public WORK nodes. A contract test asserts a won outcome demonstrably changes a subsequent match ranking.
decisions.rationale: This is the compounding edge that converts the workflow into a flywheel. v2 had all the pieces but NEVER wired the EDGE. Outcome-weighting is a validated credibility signal; async-off-the-outbox respects HDD latency. CORRECTION: the write-back DuckDB/enrichment runs in the WRITEBACK-WINDOW budget (capped memory, semaphore-gated) so it does NOT contend uncontrolled with interactive serving — the prior 'headroom' was triple-counted across burst, DuckDB, and a (now-eliminated) second vLLM process.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: No write-back (read-only graph = linear, non-compounding, no moat); synchronous write-back during editing (slow HDD graph writes on the interactive path); uncapped async DuckDB during interactive use (RAM contention); opaque outcome weighting as the sole ranker (incumbency-bias trap).
decisions.consequences: Add a Pursuit + outcome domain model and a dedicated loop-event stream; the monotonic applier (projection_version vs revocation_epoch) guarantees a re-ingest cannot resurrect a revoked/down-classified record.

decisions.title: Tiered storage: HDD cold-archive only, NVMe hot tier, RAM transient; three mutually-exclusive memory regimes
decisions.decision: Treat the spinning HDD as a COLD ARCHIVE (sequential bulk read/write of raw gzip CC0 snapshots only). An attached NVMe (PCIe Gen4 M.2, effectively mandatory in BOM) is the HOT tier for Postgres data dir + WAL, live vector/BM25/graph indexes (shared + per-tenant encrypted tablespaces), and Parquet working sets. RAM is transient + model weights + index hot pages. The box runs in ONE of three MUTUALLY-EXCLUSIVE memory regimes: SERVE, INGEST-WINDOW (serving paused / shared_buffers reduced, DuckDB memory_limit capped), WRITEBACK-WINDOW (semaphore-gated, capped). The authz/RLS hot path must NEVER incur HDD random seeks.
decisions.rationale: Orin HDD random I/O is a documented bottleneck; HNSW is pure random I/O so serving it off HDD yields 10s+ queries; per-request authz off HDD would dominate latency. DuckDB out-of-core reads HDD SEQUENTIALLY at ingest and writes Parquet to NVMe. CORRECTION: the prior single 'headroom' figure was triple-counted (burst + DuckDB spill + second vLLM); replacing it with three mutually-exclusive regime budgets makes each provably fit (see memory_budget).
decisions.alternatives_rejected: All-on-HDD (random-I/O kills query + authz latency); all-on-NVMe (raw corpora too large/expensive); in-RAM indexes only (competes with the GPU for unified 64GB); concurrent ingest+full-serve+writeback (triple-counts RAM).
decisions.consequences: BOM must include NVMe; ingestion is a controlled batch DAG in the INGEST-WINDOW; cold raw snapshots stay gzip-compressed; warm-cache-before-serve for indexes; the three regimes are documented as an operator runbook + enforced by a serving-pause/semaphore mechanism.

decisions.title: Corpus = depth-within-tenant, scoped at ingest; OpenAlex free snapshot is QUARTERLY with updated_date delta ingestion
decisions.decision: Build a deep per-tenant shared corpus (group's papers + prior winning proposals + matched funder calls) and scope public ingestion by a chosen ROR institution set and/or topic via DuckDB (NOT a full-world ingest). Integrate ORCID/SciENcv/Crossref/Grants.gov/RePORTER/NSF as periodic enrichment imports (snapshot/file readers, never metered live APIs on the hot path). The free OpenAlex snapshot is QUARTERLY; the ingestion DAG does DELTA ingestion partitioned by updated_date (download only new updated_date partitions, not a full re-ingest).
decisions.rationale: We cannot win the breadth game on one HDD-bound box vs cloud-scale incumbents, but a deep, confidential, tenant-private corpus that grounds drafting is the #1 confirmed gap in every grant-AI tool. ORCID/SciENcv alignment makes teams submission-ready (NIH-required May 2026). CORRECTION (re-verified against current OpenAlex docs, 2026): the FREE public snapshot is refreshed QUARTERLY; MONTHLY snapshots + daily changefiles require a PAID plan. (The reviewer's 'monthly is free' claim is outdated — quarterly stands for the free tier.) The valid sub-point is adopted: OpenAlex partitions by updated_date, so ingestion is incremental delta, not full re-download.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Mirroring Pivot-RP/WoS-scale corpora locally (infeasible on HDD/single box); generic LLM with no corpus grounding (commodity baseline); proprietary profile schema (ignores federal rails); full VIVO/RDF runtime (heavy for an HDD box — borrow ontology for export only); assuming monthly free cadence (factually wrong per current docs; monthly = paid).
decisions.consequences: Two grant feeds modeled distinctly (OPPORTUNITIES drive the win-loop, AWARDS feed expertise+co-funding edges); document QUARTERLY free freshness + updated_date DELTA ingestion in 09-ingestion; if monthly freshness is required, budget the PAID OpenAlex tier explicitly; commercial-OK license gate on tiered sources (PMC commercial subset only).

domain_entities.name: Tenant
domain_entities.description: A research group / institution on the one box. The unit of RLS isolation, KEK custody, encrypted-tablespace crypto-shred, and the per-tenant confidential retrieval surface. Long-term federation maps a Tenant to a node.

domain_entities.description: A person, anchored to a canonical ORCID iD. Holds memberships in one or more Tenants with roles. The node identity in the expertise graph.

domain_entities.name: TenantContext
domain_entities.description: Request-scoped frozen identity (tenant_id + subject_id + resolved Entitlement) derived from the OIDC token and pinned to the transaction via SET LOCAL. Immutable for the request.

domain_entities.description: A scholarly output node in the expertise graph, anchored by DOI, carrying SPECTER2 (precomputed-at-ingest) + retrieval embeddings. Public-tier. Also created by the write-back edge when a won proposal produces artifacts.

domain_entities.description: A historical funded project (NIH RePORTER / NSF Awards). Feeds PI track-record and co-funding collaboration edges. Public-tier.

domain_entities.description: THE loop-threading object (Instrumentl project+tracker analog). Binds a matched Opportunity -> draft Proposal -> candidate Team + ongoing match alerts. The single sticky home that creates data-gravity.

domain_entities.description: The confidential co-authored grant proposal. Lives as a CRDT buffer snapshotted (AES-GCM blob) into the KEK-bound draft store; also indexed into the OWNING tenant's confidential retrieval surface for own-tenant grounding. MAX-rule confidential tier; never enters the SHARED cross-tenant index.
domain_entities.key_fields: proposal_id, pursuit_id, owner_tenant_id, tier=confidential, crdt_doc_ref, kek_snapshot_ref, confidential_index_ref, lifecycle_state, version

domain_entities.name: ConfidentialIndexEntry
domain_entities.description: A per-tenant, RLS-isolated retrieval entry (dense vector + BM25 posting) for the tenant's OWN confidential drafts and prior winning proposals, living on the tenant's encrypted tablespace. Queryable ONLY by that tenant's confidential drafting path (PEP-enforced). Resolves the STAGE-3 grounding requirement.
domain_entities.key_fields: entry_id, tenant_id (leading index, RLS), source_proposal_id, embedding, bm25_terms, tablespace_ref

domain_entities.name: RelationTuple
domain_entities.description: The Zanzibar-style ReBAC storage row evaluated by the recursive-CTE Check() (LOCAL-only resolution; a federation-boundary rewrite). Inherits tenant RLS isolation.
domain_entities.key_fields: subject, relation, object, tenant_id (leading index)

domain_entities.name: ClassificationResult
domain_entities.description: The fail-closed classifier output gating SHARED-index ingestion. Abstention -> QUARANTINE (=confidential). Determines is_retrievable for the shared index. Walking-skeleton P0 = binary allow/quarantine.
domain_entities.key_fields: tier, decision (ALLOW/QUARANTINE/DENY), is_retrievable, class_codes[] (TEXT[]), confidence, compliance_flags[]

domain_entities.description: The ONLY shape that crosses into the SHARED/cross-tenant retrieval surface — an allowlist projection of public/private fields. The validator FORBIDS confidential. Only the broker constructs it. Carries discoverability_scope for future federation (a carry-forward-clean seam).
domain_entities.key_fields: entity_ref, tier (public|private only), fields (allowlisted), discoverability_scope (enum, future-proof), projection_version

domain_entities.name: ExpertiseFingerprint
domain_entities.description: A researcher's time-evolving expertise vector (SPECTER2 space, precomputed-at-ingest + topic weights + outcome-weighted signal). The LIVING graph signal the write-back edge mutates.
domain_entities.key_fields: subject_id, concept_weights[], specter2_centroid, outcome_weight_by_concept, last_enriched_at

domain_entities.name: CollaborationEdge (CO_PI_WITH / CO_AUTHORED)
domain_entities.description: A weighted, time-decayed collaboration edge built from co-authorship AND co-funding, plus in-platform won-proposal edges from the write-back. Powers the connectivity axis.
domain_entities.key_fields: src_subject, dst_subject, edge_type, weight, time_decay, source_proposal_id (if in-platform), award_number (if funded)

domain_entities.name: KEK / DEK (key material)
domain_entities.description: Per-tenant Key-Encryption-Key wrapping a per-tenant Data-Encryption-Key. The DEK does AES-GCM on non-searchable blobs AND unlocks the per-tenant encrypted tablespace (searchable indexes). destroy_kek() = crypto-shred for BOTH. Box-master key anchored by fTPM/passphrase (P0 default).
domain_entities.key_fields: kek_id, tenant_id, wrapped_dek, box_master_anchor_ref (fTPM PCR or passphrase-KDF), tablespace_unlock_ref, created_at, destroyed_at

domain_entities.name: AuditEvent
domain_entities.description: A per-stream hash-chained, tamper-evident security record (PEP decisions, classification, revocation, egress, grant-issued). prev_hash -> entry_hash with periodic signed checkpoints. SEPARATE from loop events.
domain_entities.key_fields: stream_id, seq, prev_hash, entry_hash, event_type, payload, ts, signed_checkpoint_ref

domain_entities.name: LoopEvent
domain_entities.description: A NON-security product-analytics event on a dedicated stream (pursuit_created, opportunity_matched, collaborator_joined[cross-tenant], first_co_edit, outcome_recorded, graph_enriched). Keeps the security audit chain clean.
domain_entities.key_fields: event_type, pursuit_id, actor_tenant_id, target_tenant_id, ts, is_cross_tenant

domain_entities.name: TombstoneLog / RevocationRecord
domain_entities.description: The owner-local durable, fsync'd revocation log. Authoritative for DENY; rebuilt on crash; refuses confidential reads until recovery completes. Revocation-by-reason (security/consent = zero allow-window).
domain_entities.key_fields: object_ref, revoked_at, reason, revocation_epoch (monotonic), committed (fsync)

security_spine.mechanism: One in-process PolicyEnforcementPoint.authorize() + data-access broker; modules import only the kernel + own subpackage (import-linter + AST test forbid raw-store/classifier-engine imports and PublishableProjection construction); broker holds raw-store creds only for shared confidential/classification tables AND per-tenant confidential-index access.
security_spine.rationale: Every retrieve/egress/derive passes one fail-closed point, so new capabilities cannot become leak vectors and a 30B builder cannot scatter enforcement logic. More critical on one box where all groups share the process. The broker is also the sole gate to the per-tenant confidential retrieval surface.

security_spine.mechanism: entitlement -> capability -> ABAC tier (in-Python lattice) -> ReBAC Check (Postgres recursive CTE, LOCAL-only) -> durable tombstone read (authoritative deny) -> short-TTL lease (narrow-only positive cache); any error/abstain DENIES; caches narrow-only; durable log authoritative for deny. The adversarial CI gates encoding this order are HUMAN-AUTHORED, not written by the 30B builder.
security_spine.rationale: Removes the fail-OPEN risk of undefined multi-store composition (convergence #1 finding); gives the builder one unambiguous order. A human authors the tripwires because they are the safety net and the model cannot be trusted to write its own.

security_spine.mechanism: FORCE RLS + AS RESTRICTIVE FOR ALL with USING + WITH CHECK on current_setting('app.tenant_id',true); tenant_id leading index; SET LOCAL via set_config(...,true) with bound param; app role NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS/NOINHERIT non-owner. Applies equally to the per-tenant confidential retrieval surface.
security_spine.rationale: Belt-and-suspenders isolation behind the PEP for many groups on one shared Postgres; SET LOCAL is leak-proof under PgBouncer transaction pooling; leading index makes the predicate an index seek (vital on the HDD box).

security_spine.mechanism: CI lint check_rls_bypass.py forbids SECURITY DEFINER, MATERIALIZED VIEW, AND VIEW over tenant tables without security_invoker=true; plus a regression test asserting NO-SET-LOCAL transaction returns ZERO rows, and a probe asserting the app role lacks BYPASSRLS/superuser.
security_spine.rationale: Closes all known RLS-bypass footguns including the VIEW vector v2 missed; the empty-GUC test guarantees fail-closed on unset tenant; the role probe stops a misconfig silently disabling the boundary.

security_spine.control: Classify-gates-index hard edge (SHARED index) + per-tenant confidential surface (own-tenant)
security_spine.mechanism: Record classified BEFORE embed/index/graph; only is_retrievable (Decision.ALLOW, public) reaches the SHARED cross-tenant sink; abstention -> QUARANTINE -> adjudication queue. SEPARATELY, own-tenant confidential drafts+prior proposals are indexed into a per-tenant RLS-isolated encrypted-tablespace surface queryable ONLY by that tenant's drafting path. The PublishableProjection validator rejects confidential tier for the SHARED index.
security_spine.rationale: Structural fail-closed enforcement at the SHARED pipeline edge for cross-tenant content; a distinct per-tenant confidential surface makes STAGE-3 own-proposal grounding (the moat) functional WITHOUT cross-tenant leakage. Proven by tenant-A-grounds / tenant-B-cannot-retrieve tests.

security_spine.control: Crypto-shred of SEARCHABLE confidential derivatives via encrypted-tablespace DEK destruction
security_spine.mechanism: Per-tenant vector/BM25/graph confidential indexes live on a per-tenant ENCRYPTED TABLESPACE / LUKS volume; crypto-shred = destroy the per-tenant DEK that unlocks the volume, then drop-and-rebuild; post-shred zero-decryptable-hits CI gate.
security_spine.rationale: AES-GCM on vectors/BM25 is mathematically unsearchable (ciphertext destroys distance metrics; encrypted postings cannot be scored), so application-layer encryption CANNOT be the mechanism for searchable indexes — encrypted-volume + DEK-destroy is the ONLY workable crypto-shred for them and is therefore PRIMARY (corrects the prior inverted design).

security_spine.control: AES-GCM ALE for NON-searchable confidential blobs
security_spine.mechanism: Per-tenant DEK does AES-256-GCM on CRDT draft snapshots, autosave, version history, eval traces, and cache VALUES before insert; destroy_kek() shreds them O(1); post-shred zero-decryptable-hits CI gate covers this path too.
security_spine.rationale: ALE is correct EXACTLY where data is never searched (opaque blobs). Scoping it to non-searchable blobs makes crypto-shred reach drafts/history/eval while leaving searchable indexes to the encrypted-tablespace mechanism — the two mechanisms together cover all confidential derivatives correctly.

security_spine.control: Box-master key custody (fTPM/passphrase P0 default; OP-TEE/EKB optional human hardening)
security_spine.mechanism: In-process LocalKms behind IKms holds per-tenant KEKs encrypted under ONE box-master key. P0 DEFAULT: box-master sealed to an fTPM PCR via userspace tpm2-tools/tpm2-pytss (no custom Trusted Application) OR derived from a boot-time passphrase via NIST SP 800-108 KDF (key never on disk). destroy_kek primitive explicit.
security_spine.rationale: The OP-TEE/EKB secure-world anchor is NOT turnkey — it needs irreversible fuse-burning + Secure Boot + a custom OP-TEE Trusted Application in C, with documented unresolved NVIDIA-forum failures — a hard wall for a Python 30B builder. The userspace fTPM/passphrase path needs no secure-world code and keeps the master key off the plaintext HDD.

security_spine.control: Confidential = local-only inference + shared-generator KV isolation (NO second model copy, NO MIG)
security_spine.mechanism: One owned tier->locality policy table consulted by BOTH the router and the egress transport (disagreement = hard-fail); confidential/private -> in-boundary vLLM ONLY, public may use cloud. KV isolation on the ONE shared 30B generator process via prefix-caching DISABLED for confidential requests (--enable-prefix-caching=False) + serialized requests with a KV boundary. NO per-tenant model duplication; MIG unavailable on Orin Ampere.
security_spine.rationale: Confidential drafts must never egress; the two-enforcement-points-one-policy-table pattern stops router/transport drift. CRITICAL: a second dedicated 30B process needs a second ~17GB+context resident copy (total ~70GB > 64GB) — infeasible. vLLM does not leak KV across separate requests by default; the real leak vector is shared-prefix caching, which we disable for confidential requests, making one shared process both safe and within budget.

security_spine.control: Owner-authoritative, fail-closed revocation with durable recovery
security_spine.mechanism: Revocation commits (fsync) to a durable revocation_log BEFORE any allow/deny observes it; crash-recovery rebuilds authorization strictly from the durable log and refuses confidential reads until recovery completes (anti-resurrection); revocation-by-reason (security/consent = zero allow-window); owner re-derives scope, caller claims are untrusted hints.
security_spine.rationale: Owner-authoritative fail-closed revocation is the correctness backbone of confidential sharing; on one box no-global-consensus is automatic, so what matters is durability + crash-recovery, proven by an injected-clock crash-mid-revocation deterministic test every CI.

security_spine.mechanism: Per-stream hash-chained AuditEvent (prev_hash -> entry_hash) in Postgres recording PEP decisions + data-access, with periodic locally-signed chain-head checkpoints; loop/product analytics kept on a SEPARATE non-security stream.
security_spine.rationale: A tamper-evident record of who accessed which group's confidential artifact under which grant is a right-sized multi-group moat and supports proving a revoked grant stopped serving; external RFC-3161/transparency-log anchoring dropped (a federation/compelled-operator concern, not a self-hosted box).

security_spine.mechanism: Entitlement/edition evaluated AT the PEP; modules physically cannot enable a capability they are not entitled to (incl. CONFIDENTIAL_RETRIEVAL on the per-tenant surface); contract test 'a lower tier cannot construct a confidential/cross-group request'.
security_spine.rationale: Keeps capability decisions in one place (a 30B builder gets scattered gates wrong); cleanly gates which groups may participate in cross-group sharing vs public-discovery-only, and who may query the confidential surface.

security_spine.control: Security-contract test suite as CI gates (HUMAN-authored)
security_spine.mechanism: Zero-leak adversarial classifier, broker-over-assert-denied, missing-ABAC-attr->deny, PIP-unavailable->deny, post-crypto-shred zero-decryptable-hits (BOTH tablespace-DEK-destroy and AES-GCM-blob paths), cross-tenant-read-denied (BOLA), confidential-surface-cross-tenant-denied, lower-tier-cannot-construct-confidential-request, crash-mid-revocation stays-denied, MAX-rule + ABAC-narrows-only property tests — all green-or-red gates. These tripwires are written by a HUMAN, not the 30B builder.
security_spine.rationale: Encodes the security spine as executable invariants rather than prose a mid-size model might ignore; the model cannot be trusted to author its own safety net, so a human writes the gates while the model writes the implementation against them.

retrieval_design: P0 retrieval is a TWO-STAGE pipeline behind ONE IRetrievalStrategy interface, with ALL three sub-stores (IVectorStore, ILexicalIndex, IGraph) backed by a SINGLE Postgres 16 instance — the headline single-box revision of v2's locked Qdrant+OpenSearch decision (those become documented future scale-out adapters, not P0 build targets). There are TWO retrieval surfaces sharing this pipeline: (A) the SHARED cross-tenant PUBLIC index (public-tier only, classify-gated), and (B) per-tenant CONFIDENTIAL retrieval surfaces on per-tenant encrypted tablespaces holding ONLY that tenant's own confidential drafts + prior winning proposals, queryable ONLY by that tenant's confidential drafting path (PEP-enforced) — this resolves the STAGE-3 grounding-vs-public-only contradiction (mod-lit-intelligence grounds drafts on BOTH A and B for the owning tenant). STAGE 1 (hybrid): dense vector search (pgvector HNSW as the VERIFIED P0 default kept RAM-resident; VectorChord IVF+RaBitQ DiskANN-style is a P1 verify-then-adopt task, NOT a P0 dependency) + native BM25 (VectorChord-BM25 — verified aarch64 via SVE SIMD + runtime CPU dispatch — or ParadeDB pg_search, whichever benchmarks well on the ACTUAL aarch64 box; no inherited x86 '3x-vs-ES' claim is relied upon) fused with RRF k=60 in SQL. RRF is chosen because it is parameter-free, score-scale-immune, and needs ZERO labeled data — correct for a fresh deployment; learned/convex fusion deferred until per-tenant labels exist. BM25 is NON-optional: scholarly+grant queries are entity-heavy (author/lab names, grant/solicitation numbers, gene/method acronyms). STAGE 2 (rerank): a local cross-encoder reranks top-50 -> top-8 (bge-reranker-v2-m3 568M or Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B) via a dedicated vLLM score-endpoint process (sentence-transformers in-process fallback, which saves a CUDA context); rerank adds +5-15 nDCG@10 for <200ms; two-stage beats single-stage (Recall@5 0.816 vs 0.695). EMBEDDINGS: bge-m3 (dense+sparse+ColBERT, 8192 ctx) or Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B as the SINGLE serve-time retriever embedder; SPECTER2 (Apache-2.0, base+proximity adapter via the `adapters` library) is a SECOND citation-aware space for paper-similarity / expertise fingerprints — PRECOMPUTED AT INGEST as a batch job then UNLOADED (NOT serve-resident, NOT served by vLLM), so it appears only in the ingest-window memory budget. CHUNKING: section-aware splitting + hierarchical parent/child (embed 128-256 tok children, return 512-1024 tok parents); semantic/LLM chunking SKIPPED at P0 (NAACL 2025: fixed ~200-word chunks match/beat it). QUERY EXPANSION / AGENTIC: P0 is single-shot hybrid+rerank ONLY; P1 adds an Adaptive-RAG difficulty router that conditionally triggers HyDE/multi-query (each an extra LLM call contending for the one GPU, off by default) and a CRAG corrective loop on the proposal-grounding path; multi-agent decomposition reserved for team-assembly. GRAPH: a deterministic metadata-backbone edge table (authors/papers/citations/affiliations/venues/grants/topics) built from corpus metadata with NO recurring LLM entity-extraction tax — this same graph IS the collaborator-discovery product surface; bounded-hop recursive CTEs do traversal; HippoRAG2-style Personalized-PageRank graph-augmented retrieval (~1k tokens/query) is a P1 SQL/Python add (Microsoft GraphRAG global summarization ~331k tokens/query rejected as infeasible on edge; Apache AGE rejected). EVAL: RAGAS faithfulness + context precision/recall + nDCG@k/Recall@k on a small per-tenant gold set, wired into CI as a regression gate, with an IN-BOUNDARY local 30B judge (mandatory — confidential drafts forbid a cloud judge); eval artifacts are confidential-tier (AES-GCM blob, crypto-shred on erasure). BENCHMARK ACCEPTANCE: P0.5 includes a test that benchmarks BM25 latency on the REAL aarch64 box (not an inherited x86 number). HDD GUARDRAIL (load-bearing): the live HNSW index must NEVER be served off the spinning HDD; the index lives RAM-resident / on NVMe, Postgres data+WAL on NVMe, HDD restricted to sequential cold-blob reads at ingestion only. PARTIAL-FAILURE POLICY: public/shared discovery returns partial-results-with-honest-completeness-indicator (never whole-query-fail); the confidential path is whole-query-fail-closed.
memory_budget: Single Orin AGX 64GB LPDDR5 UNIFIED memory (CPU+GPU share one pool — the hard ceiling for ALL processes COMBINED). The prior single 'headroom' figure was TRIPLE-COUNTED (burst + DuckDB spill + a now-ELIMINATED second vLLM process). It is replaced by THREE MUTUALLY-EXCLUSIVE regime budgets, each proven to fit. === REGIME 1: SERVE (interactive steady state) === (1) OS + L4T + CUDA drivers + headroom ~7GB. (2) GENERATOR process — Qwen3-30B-A3B INT4/W4A16, weights ~17GB (ALL 30.5B experts resident; the 3.3B active-per-token governs only DECODE SPEED ~30-45 tok/s, not footprint) + KV cache/activations/CUDA context @ ~20k ctx, small max-num-seqs ~8GB = ~25GB. (3) EMBEDDER process — bge-m3 568M FP16 weights ~1.2GB + CUDA context ~1.3GB = ~2.5GB. (4) RERANKER process — bge-reranker-v2-m3 568M weights ~1.2GB + CUDA context ~1.3GB = ~2.5GB. (5) SPECTER2 = 0GB (precomputed at ingest, UNLOADED at serve). (6) Postgres shared_buffers + OS page cache for the hot pgvector HNSW + BM25 index (scoped tenant corpus ~100K-1M chunks at 1024-dim + HNSW ~1.5-2x overhead; shared public + the small hot per-tenant confidential surfaces) ~7GB. (7) Postgres backends + PgBouncer + FastAPI + Python workers + CRDT websocket server (CRDT docs KB-MB, negligible) ~5GB. SERVE TOTAL = 7+25+2.5+2.5+0+7+5 = ~49GB, leaving ~15GB margin. RECOMMENDED SAVER: collapse embedder+reranker to sentence-transformers IN-PROCESS (drops 2 CUDA contexts ~2.6GB) -> ~46GB. CONFIDENTIAL DRAFTING adds NO resident model copy — it reuses the SAME generator process with --enable-prefix-caching=False + serialized requests (D10), so SERVE total is unchanged at ~49GB. (If true PROCESS isolation is ever mandated, the confidential process loads Qwen3-14B ~9GB weights + ~4GB context = ~13GB AND the public 30B is PAUSED/EVICTED first: 7 + 13 + 2.5 + 2.5 + 7 + 5 = ~37GB — NEVER two 30B copies, NEVER 70GB.) === REGIME 2: INGEST-WINDOW (bulk DuckDB load; interactive serving PAUSED, generator evicted or idle) === OS+drivers ~7GB; generator EVICTED (0GB) [or idle-resident ~17GB if a quick window]; DuckDB out-of-core with SET memory_limit='8GB' + capped threads ~8GB; SPECTER2 batch (base+proximity adapter, loaded only here) ~1.5GB; embedder process for chunk embeddings ~2.5GB; Postgres with REDUCED shared_buffers during bulk load + writer backends ~6GB. INGEST TOTAL (generator evicted) = 7+8+1.5+2.5+6 = ~25GB (huge margin); (generator idle-resident) = ~42GB. Fits either way. === REGIME 3: WRITEBACK-WINDOW (async loop enrichment, SEMAPHORE-GATED to yield to interactive generation) === SERVE baseline ~49GB + capped writeback DuckDB/enrichment (SET memory_limit='4GB') + SPECTER2 reload for fingerprint recompute ~1.5GB = ~54.5GB, within 64GB; the semaphore ensures writeback and an interactive generation burst do not both peak. === CONTENTION RULES === (a) the box is in exactly ONE regime at a time; ingestion (P0.7) runs in a maintenance window with serving paused; (b) serialize LLM generation vs heavy embedding batches; gate generation so the CRDT editor stays responsive; (c) confidential KV isolation = prefix-caching-off + serialization on the ONE shared generator, NO MIG (Orin Ampere lacks MIG; deferred to Thor/Blackwell). === DATA PLACEMENT === spinning HDD = COLD ARCHIVE only — raw CC0 snapshots gzip-compressed, read SEQUENTIALLY at ingestion (OpenAlex ~330GB gz scoped by ROR/topic via DuckDB, QUARTERLY free snapshot with updated_date DELTA ingestion; Crossref ~200GB via Academic Torrents; ORCID anchors-only from the ~730GB-uncompressed summaries; full small sources ROR/NSF/NIH/Grants.gov); NVMe (PCIe Gen4 M.2, effectively MANDATORY in BOM) = HOT tier for Postgres data dir + WAL + live shared/confidential indexes + Parquet working sets; RAM = transient + model weights + index hot pages. If a dense 32B were chosen, weights rise to ~19GB AND decode slows — a second reason the A3B MoE is correct.

open_risks.risk: vLLM SM 8.7 community wheel drifts from JetPack/CUDA versions or the builder uses default-PyPI vllm (CPU fallback / silent failure) across the THREE vLLM processes.
open_risks.mitigation: PIN exact JetPack 6.2/CUDA 12.6/Python/vLLM versions verbatim; add a startup assertion that loaded torch/vllm reports SM 8.7 CUDA in EACH process; document llama.cpp (LLM) + sentence-transformers (embed/rerank) fallbacks; NEVER pip install vllm from default PyPI; prefer the sentence-transformers-in-process saver if the 3-process build is fragile.

open_risks.risk: Confidential drafting KV isolation is mis-implemented (prefix caching left ON for confidential requests) -> shared-prefix KV leak; OR someone reintroduces a second 30B process and blows the 64GB ceiling.
open_risks.mitigation: Enforce --enable-prefix-caching=False on the confidential path with a startup/route assertion; HUMAN-authored test that a confidential request does not reuse a cached prefix; document in CONVENTIONS that a second resident 30B copy is FORBIDDEN (use prefix-off+serialization, or Qwen3-14B WITH the 30B evicted); a CI/runtime probe asserts SERVE-regime resident memory <= ~49GB.

open_risks.risk: Crypto-shred mis-built: builder applies AES-GCM to vectors/BM25 (unsearchable -> broken confidential grounding) instead of encrypted-tablespace DEK destruction.
open_risks.mitigation: CONVENTIONS states the SPLIT explicitly (encrypted-tablespace+DEK-destroy for SEARCHABLE indexes; AES-GCM only for NON-searchable blobs); P0.4b builds the searchable path AFTER P0.5; HUMAN-authored zero-decryptable-hits gates cover BOTH paths; a test asserts the confidential vector surface remains SEARCHABLE while mounted.

open_risks.risk: OP-TEE/EKB hardware key anchor becomes a hard build wall (irreversible fuse-burn + secure-world C, documented NVIDIA-forum failures).
open_risks.mitigation: P0 default is the USERSPACE fTPM (tpm2-tools, no custom TA) or passphrase-KDF master key; OP-TEE/EKB is documented as OPTIONAL human-operator hardening (out of scope for the automated build) behind the SAME IKms; state plainly that fuse-burning Secure Boot is irreversible.

open_risks.risk: Outcome-weighted graph write-back entrenches established investigators (incumbency bias).
open_risks.mitigation: Keep outcome weight TRANSPARENT and as ONE signal among expertise-similarity and connectivity, never the sole ranker; surface per-candidate 'why'; allow PI curation; expose a tunable weight and log its influence on rankings.

open_risks.risk: CRDT confidential draft leaks via autosave/version-history/synthesizer buffers that bypass the encrypted store.
open_risks.mitigation: MAX-rule-tag the generated draft, autosave, and history as confidential and persist them ONLY via AES-GCM blob encryption in the per-tenant KEK-bound store; snapshot the CRDT doc on autosave intervals (not per-keystroke); HUMAN-authored test that no draft artifact lands in a non-encrypted store.

open_risks.risk: A 30B builder mis-implements the multi-store decision composition and creates a fail-OPEN path, OR writes weak adversarial tests for its own safety net.
open_risks.mitigation: Fix ONE decision order in the kernel docs + a single PEP function; encode it as failing-if-violated CI gates AUTHORED BY A HUMAN (any-step-error->deny, lower-tier-cannot-construct, PIP-unavailable->deny); forbid scattering authz logic via import-linter; keep the order in CONVENTIONS as 'this file wins'.

open_risks.risk: Phase-0 scope overwhelms a mid-size local builder (full security kernel + retrieval + router + ingestion + CRDT + write-back).
open_risks.mitigation: Sequence as a WALKING SKELETON: prove the loop end-to-end on the simplest substrate (one tenant pair, real-time editing only, binary allow/quarantine, drop-tablespace crypto-shred, single embedding space, HNSW only). Defer to P1: suggesting-mode, anchored comments, HippoRAG2, probabilistic identity blocking, the OP-TEE hardware anchor, RaBitQ >RAM index. Humans author the security CI tripwires.

open_risks.risk: DuckDB + Postgres + vLLM RAM contention at ingest/writeback time (the prior 'headroom' was triple-counted).
open_risks.mitigation: THREE mutually-exclusive regimes (SERVE / INGEST-WINDOW / WRITEBACK-WINDOW): bulk ingestion runs serving-paused; DuckDB capped via SET memory_limit (8GB ingest, 4GB writeback) + capped threads; writeback gated behind a semaphore that yields to interactive generation; each regime's budget shown to fit (memory_budget).

open_risks.risk: Single box = single point of failure (no HA); a disk or power loss loses live state.
open_risks.mitigation: Postgres data+WAL on NVMe with synchronous_commit=on + local WAL+PITR backups to the HDD cold tier; durable fsync'd revocation log with rebuild-from-log recovery (refuse confidential reads until recovery completes); document RPO/RTO honestly as single-box pilot-scale.

open_risks.risk: Builder reintroduces dropped/federation tech (OPA daemon, SpiceDB cluster, CloudHSM, MIG, second 30B process, Qdrant+OpenSearch, ALE-on-vectors) by following un-revised v2/CONVENTIONS docs.
open_risks.mitigation: Author a single-box CONVENTIONS that REVISES the contested pins (ABAC=in-Python, ReBAC=Postgres-CTE, KMS=LocalKms+fTPM/passphrase, retrieval=single-Postgres, GPU-isolation=prefix-off-on-one-process-not-MIG-not-second-copy, crypto-shred=encrypted-tablespace-for-searchable + AES-GCM-for-blobs, serving=3-vLLM-processes-or-ST-saver) and states 'this file wins'; cite the ARM64/Orin evidence inline.

open_risks.risk: License contamination: a non-commercial PMC article or ODC-BY S2 data reaches a commercial feature, or confidential drafts mix with public CC0 records.
open_risks.mitigation: Carry a per-record provenance+license tag on every ingested entity; fail-closed commercial-use gate ingests only PMC 'Commercial Use Allowed'; store the ODC-BY attribution string with derived data; classification + RLS + the separate confidential surface keep confidential drafts physically separate from public corpus.
